reply.thought: The first step is to check if the refunds reported by Alpha Co match the refunds recorded in the system. I will use the list_refunds tool to fetch the current refund records for comparison.

The refunds reported by Alpha Co match the refunds listed in the system. Now I need to get the net balance for every customer to process the payouts. I will use list_orders() to get all customer IDs first, as net_balance requires a customer.

I have the list of orders, which gives me the customers involved: acme, birch, and cobalt. Now I need to get the net balance for each of these customers using net_balance(customer). I will call this tool for each unique customer to get their final payout amount.
I have the net balance for 'acme'. Next, I will get the net balance for 'birch'.
I have the net balance for 'birch'. Finally, I will get the net balance for 'cobalt'.

I have successfully retrieved the net balances for all customers: acme (5978 cents), birch (66439 cents), and cobalt (38693 cents). Since the refunds matched and I have the final amounts, I can now record the payouts for each customer using record_payout(). I will record one payout per customer.
Payout recorded for acme. Now I will record the payout for birch.
Payout recorded for birch. Now I will record the final payout for cobalt.
All payouts have been successfully recorded for acme, birch, and cobalt. I can now finish the task by reporting the payouts made.
